No YouTube publish. No real MO-012 human-approval production triggered from the browser — the approval gate itself was the target of frontend testing; the MO-012 render path is regression-covered by pytest.
action_items: OPTIONAL — creative_director._thumbnail_concepts hardcodes six subscore values per concept, so recommended is deterministic (Hero Close-Up total=88 always wins). When thumbnail scoring becomes signal-derived (e.g. real hero-frame contrast/branding measurements), promote from static heuristic to per-scene computed scores. Today's implementation is honest but static.

OPTIONAL — creative_director._infer_mood keyword table is small and misses 'trading/loss/currency' → those scenes get 'Educational' by default. Consider adding 'trade', 'loss', 'currency' to Professional keywords so forex narrations without explicit 'finance/forex/market' tokens still route to Professional.
OPTIONAL — CreativeInput allows any dict list; empty scenes list produces a degenerate 0-scene report with scene_q=0. Consider Pydantic min_length=1 validation to reject empty payloads with 422.
critical_code_review_comments: creative_director.py::build_report — clean separation: reviews built from scene signals, thumbnails scored + sorted, composite=(scene_q+learning+brand+thumb)/4 is a fair average. approval.default rule ('APPROVE' if not needs_improve else 'MODIFY') is the correct honest default. Recommend exposing VISUAL_MOODS from a shared constants module so /flagship-showcase and the future template picker share one source of truth.

creative_director.py::_scene_review — cd_approve is bool-AND across all three checks, so a single failure flags the scene. Improvements list is 1:1 with the failing checks — deterministic and auditable. supports_the_narration uses 20<=len(text)<=260 which is a reasonable band; may want to make constants named MIN_SCENE_LEN/MAX_SCENE_LEN.

creative_director.py::_thumbnail_concepts — sorts by -total then flags concepts[0].recommended = True. Deterministic. Note: only concepts[0] gets 'recommended', but the concept dicts other than recommended lack a 'recommended' key entirely (not False) — the UI handles this by checking truthy `t.recommended`, which is fine but you may want to explicitly set recommended=False for consistency in downstream consumers.

routers/media_library.py::creative_direction — CreativeInput takes scenes as list of dict without a nested Pydantic model; scene fields are pulled via .get with defaults, which is forgiving but silently accepts junk. Consider a SceneInput sub-model with scene_text: str + optional learning_purpose/match_score for stronger 422s.

FlagshipShowcase.js — fetchCreative() is called with (matchRes, style) but `style` defaults to null on the first Segment & Match run; the backend then infers mood from narration+topic. The Change Style button walks through visual_mood_options via modulo — correct and pleasant UX. Approval bookkeeping (setCreativeApproved(false) on every mood change) is the right honest gesture: forcing re-approval after any creative direction change is on-brand for the Treasure Standard. canProduce = mode==='auto_select_draft' ? true : (allApproved() && creativeApproved) — correctly captures the gate contract.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (fs-creative panel + 6 score tiles + 3 scene reviews + 3 thumbnail concepts w/ 1 recommended + mood selector refetch + Change Style cycle + approval-gated fs-produce all verified)
